Evidence.description:
A concrete piece of support for a vulnerability judgement.

Every Finding must bind at least one Evidence. Evidence can be a source
snippet, a call chain, a taint path, decompiled pseudocode, a tool-output
summary, a crash input, a PoC description, or a SARIF location. The
``produced_by_*`` fields keep evidence traceable back to the run/tool that
created it.
Evidence.title: Evidence

ExecutionJob.description:
Durable control-plane state for one bounded backend execution.

``request`` is the persisted, redacted request view. The exact live request
is intentionally kept only by the in-process controller until a durable
secret-reference/worker transport is configured.
ExecutionJob.title: ExecutionJob

ExecutionRequest.description:
A structured tool execution request.

``command`` is modeled for future backends, but the default Local backend
does not execute arbitrary shell. Tool adapters should prefer structured
``args`` over raw command strings.
ExecutionRequest.title: ExecutionRequest

ExecutionResult.description: Structured result returned by an ExecutionBackend.
ExecutionResult.title: ExecutionResult

Fact.description:
A confirmed fact. **Facts are append-only: they are never mutated.**

State changes are expressed by appending *new* Facts. Origin and Goal facts
are special-cased via ``node_type`` so the graph always has a start and a
target. ``derived_from`` records the Facts/Intents/Evidence that produced
this Fact, which is what makes the audit replayable.
Fact.title: Fact

Finding.description:
A vulnerability finding.

Invariant: a Finding **must** reference at least one Evidence id. The
Observer is responsible for moving findings between statuses (candidate ->
confirmed / needs_review / false_positive / duplicate). ``fingerprint`` is
used by the manager for dedup, and ``dedup_of`` points a duplicate at its
canonical finding.
Finding.title: Finding

FindingRetest.description:
A retest attempt against one finding.

Invariants: at most one open retest per finding; the conclusion is write-once; and only a normally completed retest with verdict `fixed` may rewrite the finding status.

assessment.description: Raw advisor text, kept when no verdict could be parsed.
assessment.title: Assessment

context_source.title: Context Source

verdict.description: Wire value of RetestVerdict; empty until a verdict was parsed.
verdict.title: Verdict

Natural language is classified into one of these values at intake time.
The termination state machine consumes only this structured contract and
never tries to rediscover intent from words in the user prompt.
GoalOutcomeType.title: GoalOutcomeType

When the corpus is empty, the CLI is unavailable, or no citation could be
parsed, ``status`` reflects the no-hit reason and ``answer`` is left empty
(or replaced by an explicit ``no_hit_gap``). The platform MUST NOT fabricate
knowledge-graph content.

Hint.description:

heap bugs". Hints influence Intent generation and prompt context only; they
must never be cited as Evidence for a Finding.

An exploration intent.

An Intent starts from one or more Facts and aims to produce new Facts,
Evidence, or Findings (e.g. "trace the `filename` param of /api/upload",
"check stack bounds in sub_401230"). The ``solver`` hint lets the manager
route the intent to the right Solver; ``priority`` orders the work queue.
